evidence.text:
Problem definition
Many material properties can be derived from the fundamental equations
of electronic behavior, where the dynamics of electrons are fully determined by the external po-
tential imposed by the atomic arrangement in a crystal (Martin, 2020). Crystal property predic-
tion thus aims to estimate a physical property y from the crystal structure, represented as a tuple
(A, P, L). The target property y may be continuous (y ∈R) in regression tasks or categorical
(y ∈{1, 2, . . . , C}) in classification tasks with C classes.

The successful construction of a stable Ni cluster catalyst has enabled a H2 production rate (500 °C, 279.2 mmolH2·gNi−1·min−1) and exceptional thermal stability.
The formation process and underlying mechanism of stable Ni clusters are elucidated.

objective: improve accuracy of a pretrained MLIP for a specific system while preserving its generalizability and preventing catastrophic forgetting
material_scope: non-argyrodite-type materials (sulfides, oxides, nitrides, halides, hydrides)
constraints: enable knowledge transfer to chemically distinct systems
input_requirements: pretrained dataset (MPtrj) for Replay and FIM computation
output_goal: forgetting-aware fine-tuned MLIP model (reEWC) with improved PES accuracy and preserved generalizability

evidence.text: Herein, we propose reEWC, an advanced fine-tuning strategy that integrates Experience Replay and Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) to effectively balance forgetting prevention with fine-tuning efficiency.

task_name_raw: creation of an open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells
objective: to expand the normal research cycle by collecting all perovskite solar cell data, both past and future, in one place; to make all historical data accessible and provide means to upload new experimental data; to implement interactive graphical data visualization tools that enable simple and interactive exploration, analysis and filtering
constraints: FAIR data principles (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable)
input_requirements: peer-reviewed papers on metal-halide perovskite solar cells
output_goal: open-access database containing >42,400 photovoltaic devices
free interactive web-based tools for exploration, analysis, filtering and visualization
open-source code base
procedures and protocols for FAIR-compliant data dissemination

evidence.text: Here we extract all the meaningful device data from peer-reviewed papers on metal-halide perovskite solar cells published so far and make them available in a database. We collect data from over 42,400 photovoltaic devices with up to 100 parameters per device. We then develop open-source and accessible procedures to analyse the data, providing examples of insights that can be gleaned from the analysis of a large dataset. The database, graphics and analysis tools are made available to the community and will continue to evolve as an open-source initiative.

task_name_raw: ML-based correction of DFT formation enthalpy errors for improved phase stability prediction
objective: To systematically correct intrinsic energy resolution errors in DFT-calculated formation enthalpies to improve the reliability of first-principles predictions of phase stability, particularly in ternary systems.
output_goal: corrected formation enthalpy (Hpred = HDFT − Hcorr)
reduced RMSE in formation enthalpy prediction (from ~41 meV/atom to ~10 meV/atom)

evidence.text: In this work, we present a machine learning (ML) approach to systematically correct these errors, improving the reliability of first-principles predictions. A neural network model has been trained to predict the discrepancy between DFT-calculated and experimentally measured enthalpies for binary and ternary alloys and compounds.
The purpose of this work is to outline a way to reduce this error.

We have investigated a machine learning-based approach and its ability to enhance the accuracy of density functional theory (DFT) calculations for alloy formation enthalpies, particularly in ternary phase stability calculations.
